findings.rationale: Duplicate-write detection collapses every field lvalue to InitWriteKey::Root. Consequently valid component-wise initialization such as assigning two distinct fields of one struct is rejected as assigning the state variable twice, even though the coverage machinery is explicitly designed to merge distinct field assignments.

Refinement initial-state enumeration treats a root as assigned if any component is written on any branch. Unwritten map keys, struct fields, and conditionally unwritten components are therefore defaulted instead of enumerated. This can omit legal initial valuations and yield an unsound refinement result; when no whole root is free, the deterministic Monitor constructor rejects the model instead.

check_refinement claims to support nondeterministic abstract initialization and enumerates its initial states, but subsequently constructs abstract monitors with Monitor::new, which requires deterministic initialization. Any abstraction with a genuinely free initial variable therefore errors before membership or transition checks; the already available from_state constructor is required here.

The document conformance checker accepts V2 signed approval records, extracts their binding and key ID, and renders them into the expected artifact without verifying the signature or consulting a trust store. A forged or modified signed approval can therefore be presented with a matching forged document and reported as document_conformant.

Document generation populates AppliedApproval.artifact_digest from target.reviewed_digest, while document checking reconstructs the same overlay using target.digest. For requirements-document approvals these represent different artifacts, so a legitimately generated approved document can be reconstructed differently and falsely reported as drifted.

The approval check exit status is nonzero only for signature-invalid. Other negative statuses produced by approval::evaluate, such as stale or drifted bindings, are returned with exit code 0, so CI gates can pass an approval that the command itself reports as no longer current.

A dataset source declared in an AI project is converted directly to PathBuf and thus resolved against the process working directory rather than the project file's parent. The same project succeeds or fails depending on the caller's current directory unless --records is supplied.

The explanation walker ignores function-call arguments and binder expressions. Those expressions are evaluated in the action context and can contain division, remainder, or partial sequence operations, so generated auto_checks and explanations omit real partial-operation sites such as f(1 / x) or a partial forall range/filter.
